key_decisions.rationale: Keeps emphatic benefit, priority, communal stewardship, and divine oracles.
key_decisions.before: Much in every way. First of all, they were entrusted with God’s words.
key_decisions.after: Much in every way! First of all, the Jewish people were entrusted with the words of God.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Much in every way. To begin with, they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves limited “some,” faith/unfaithfulness wordplay, rhetorical question, and divine fidelity.
key_decisions.before: What if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness cancel God’s faithfulness?
key_decisions.after: What if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God's faithfulness?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: What if some were unfaithful? Does their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps emphatic rejection, God/human contrast, Scripture, vindication, speech, and judgment.
key_decisions.before: Absolutely not! Let God be true even if every human being is a liar, as it is written, “So that you may be shown right in your words and prevail when you are judged.”
key_decisions.after: Absolutely not! Let God be shown true, even if every human is a liar, as it is written: “So that you may be proved right in your words and prevail when you are judged.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By no means! Let God be shown to be true, though every human being a liar, as it is written, “So that you may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves debated self-reference, emphatic denial, prior accusation, both groups, universality, and sin's dominion.

key_decisions.after: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already charged that both Jewish and Greek people are all under sin,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: What then? Are we any better off? Not at all. For we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under the power of sin,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps comprehensive humanity, justification, divine presence, works, Law, and sin-awareness.

key_decisions.after: For no human being will be declared righteous before him by works of the Law, since through the Law comes knowledge of sin.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For no human being will be set right in God’s sight by works of the law, since through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps God as agent, debated hilastērion imagery with a note, faith, blood, demonstration, restraint, and former sins.
key_decisions.before: God presented him as a place of atonement by his blood, received through trust. This was to demonstrate God’s righteousness, because in his restraint God had passed over sins committed beforehand.
key_decisions.after: God presented him as an atoning sacrifice, effective through faith in his blood, to demonstrate God's righteousness, because in his restraint he had passed over sins committed beforehand.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: whom God put forward as a place of atonement by his blood, to be received through trust. This was to show God’s righteousness, because in divine forbearance God had passed over former sins;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves purpose, repeated demonstration, current time, God's justice, justification, and faith relation.
key_decisions.before: It was to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so that God may be just and the one who sets right the person who lives from Jesus’ faithfulness.
key_decisions.after: He did this to demonstrate his righteousness in the present time, so that he might be righteous and declare righteous the one who has faith in Jesus.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: it was to show God’s righteousness at the present time, so that God may be shown to be just and the one who sets right those who live from the faithfulness of Jesus.
